prize_parts.citation: for showing how collateral constraints tie credit limits to asset prices, so that small shocks are amplified and propagated into persistent credit cycles and economic downturns

statement.case_for: My configuration changed in one respect and stayed the same in another. I still prefer B004 as a single part. I now credit only Kiyotaki and Moore, where in round 1 I added Gertler. The discovery I would reward is the collateral-constraint mechanism: a durable, pledgeable asset links borrowing limits to asset prices, and that feedback turns a small shock into a persistent downturn. Kiyotaki and Moore (1997) originated it, and no colleague disputes that. The mechanism has about three decades of extension, estimation and policy use behind it, and the 2007-09 crisis tested its relevance. It is conceptually original, tractable to state in a citation, and the pair is exactly the unit the discussion has called the clean core. What moved me was the attribution argument, not a count of supporters. The credit for Gertler I proposed rests on his intermediary-finance work with Kiyotaki. Under a three-name cap and a single-discovery citation, I cannot separate that work cleanly from the Bernanke-Gertler accelerator strand that the 2022 prize touched, or from Gertler's role in B015. My round-1 file said the pair would be the better citation if that separation could not be made. After reading Hassler, Strömberg and Enflo, I judge that it cannot be made without a longer citation than a single discovery supports. I would sooner credit a narrower, defensible discovery than a broader one whose edge is contested.
statement.case_against: The pair leaves the quantitative intermediary strand and Gilchrist's empirical work uncredited. A committee could judge that this understates how the mechanism reached policy analysis after 2008. Overlap with the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises remains the main objection to B004 even for the pair, because the committee may regard financial frictions as already recognised. Much of the aggregate evidence is calibrated or indirect, not cleanly identified, as Hjalmarsson and Strömberg both note. The mechanism is also theoretical and validated mainly through its absorption into later work, so a committee that weights design-based evidence more heavily could prefer B002. A committee that weights maturity and a concentrated joint core could prefer B027. I rely on general knowledge, not independent verification of citations.

responses.point: Hassler sees Kiyotaki-Moore as the clear two-person core. He proposed only that pair for B004 because of the Bernanke overlap. He warned that a two-name award leaves the financial-accelerator strand uncredited and that the committee should say so explicitly.
responses.response: I now follow your attribution. The citation should say what it rewards, namely the collateral-constraint feedback between credit limits and asset prices, and it should not suggest that it covers the accelerator or intermediary strands. I accept your point that this is a deliberate narrowing, and I would write it into the citation. My ordering of B004 against B015 does not depend on novelty alone. B004 offers a pair with a clean origin. B015 requires a three-name cut among eight names with no agreed originator criterion in the exchange, and I still weight that heavily.

responses.point: Strömberg keeps Gertler as a third laureate for the intermediary-balance-sheet work with Kiyotaki, and says he would not strongly object to the pair. He asks that the choice rest on the attribution argument.
responses.response: That is the argument I have tried to apply, and I move away from you on it. I do not doubt that the Gertler-Kiyotaki intermediary work is a real step. My difficulty is that it is a second contribution, and it sits next to the part of Gertler's record the 2022 prize addressed and next to his B015 credit. Putting it in one citation would need a sentence the evidence here does not let me defend. If the Committee reads the intermediary strand as separable, your trio is the best alternative inside B004, and I would not call it unreasonable. As a first choice I prefer the pair, because it is the narrower claim and the one we all agree on.

responses.point: Enflo lists B004 as an alternative. In her reply to Strömberg she says a Kiyotaki-Moore pair, or a pair plus Gertler, looks more defensible than her first trio. She keeps B004 because the mechanism is foundational and well tested after 2008, and is less sure of its marginal novelty given 2022.
responses.response: We agree on attribution, and I take the novelty doubt seriously, because it applies to the pair as much as to the trio. My answer is that the 2022 prize was about banks and financial crises as an empirical and theoretical object. The Kiyotaki-Moore mechanism is a different result: it shows how asset prices and credit limits reinforce each other in a general-equilibrium setting. I would not claim the two are unrelated. I would claim that the pair does not duplicate the prior recognition. I also take your symmetry remark, since B027 faces a comparable proximity question from 2024, and I do not treat proximity as decisive for either.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson ranks B002 first. She argues that replication and extension with other administrative datasets support the measurement advance and the exposure-based designs. She says the unresolved questions concern the size of specific causal place effects. She would accept B002 waiting if the committee thinks a decade is too short.
responses.response: In reply to the chair's question, here is what would settle the maturity issue for me. I would look for replication of the exposure-effect estimates in non-US administrative data and for long-run follow-up of the exposed cohorts. A citation limited to measurement and exposure-based designs, which you propose, would answer most of my concern. It is a more defensible citation than the broader one. I still place B002 behind B004 and B027 because I weigh maturity above design credibility when the evidence is still accumulating. That is a judgement about timing, not a verdict on merit, and I keep B002 as an alternative. Your point that the trio is well defined and the Katz question is the open one seems right to me.

responses.point: Krusell defends the Calvo-Taylor-Woodford trio for B015 as originators of separate building blocks. He admits that the three-name cap may do real injustice to colleagues, and he asks that his alternatives be read as sincere.
responses.response: I accept that originators versus developers is a coherent criterion, and it answers part of my attribution objection. It does not remove it. The criterion has to be accepted by the committee, and the exchange shows that Hassler, Krusell and Boppart apply it differently, since some openings propose Gali and others do not. My eighth-place ranking of B015 reflected that, and I am not changing it. I also note your remark that you and the chair are long-time co-authors, and I do not treat your agreement as independent evidence. I treat the substance of your reply as useful, particularly the point that the post-2021 inflation debate concerns forecasting and supply shocks more than the pricing mechanism.

uncertainties: Whether the committee regards the 2022 prize as having covered the financial-friction agenda enough to make even the Kiyotaki-Moore pair redundant.
Whether the intermediary-finance strand is separable enough from the Bernanke-Gertler accelerator and from B015 to justify adding Gertler. If it is, the trio would be the better citation.
How much indirect or calibrated aggregate evidence should count against a mechanism that is conceptually strong, compared with the design-based evidence in B002.
Whether B027's thematic proximity to the 2024 prize is a scientific consideration or only one of timing, and whether the pair or the trio is the right attribution there.
Whether replication and long-run follow-up for B002 will settle the causal place-effect claims soon, and which of the three names an argument for Katz would displace.
My assessments rely on general knowledge of the literature and the supplied round-1 files, and I have not independently verified citations.
statement.conflict_note: No change. The supplied profile shows no co-authorship or institutional tie to Kiyotaki, Moore, Gertler or Gilchrist, and none to the B027 or B002 names. My field is market and mechanism design, which is not adjacent to the collateral-constraint literature. I disclose my SSE affiliate status alongside the committee members Dreber Almenberg, Friberg and Strömberg, and my Lund affiliation shared with Enflo. None of these is a link to a shortlisted candidate, and I do not adjudicate any of them. I will treat the connections the chair listed among Hassler, Krusell, Boppart and Friberg as disclosures only. They did not affect how I weighed the replies above.
